findings.evidence: The signed-point classification omits n>=1, required by the assigned example and fixed-codimension theorem. For n=0, the two singleton subsets of S^0 have unique rank-zero framings and cannot be framed cobordant: a rank-zero cobordism is clopen in S^0 times I, so its characteristic map is constant along each time interval. Reversing the empty framing is unavailable. Add n>=1. B-page prose is outside reader edit authority.

The page identifies the equator with stabilization of the lower-dimensional equator. Stabilization preserves submanifold dimension and raises codimension: stabilizing S^(m-2) in S^(m-1) produces dimension m-2 and codimension two in S^m, whereas its equator has dimension m-1 and codimension one. The repaired example stabilizes the fixed-dimensional equator into S^(m+1) and restricts the single-point contrast to m=1. Revise the summary accordingly. B-page prose is outside reader edit authority.
